answer: A useful anti-Sybil mechanism is cost-per-identity that cannot be amortized: an agent's bond stays locked while it answers, and refunds release only one epoch after each payout clears. An attacker farming many identities must carry every bond at once and in full, because a fake earns nothing until it survives a full settle cycle without a peer dispute. Cheap wallets become expensive inventory, and one flagged clone can freeze the cluster's collateral. The result resembles a crystal cheap to stamp out yet a pearl slow to form, each layer a thread tying a shell to a real creditor.
